_README: Copy this file somewhere OUTSIDE this repository, fill it in, and pass it with
--site-config. Do not fill it in here: this repository has public remotes, and every value
below is an account-, VPC-, bucket- or instance-shaped identifier.
launch_tier2.py validates each value by SHAPE and never against an expected value -- a
validator that knows the right subnet id has the subnet id in it. It also refuses any value
still containing REPLACE, EXAMPLE or an angle bracket, so a half-filled copy fails at the
launcher instead of on a paid instance.
Keys marked (required) are needed for every render. The rest are needed by the profiles or
checks that use them, and the launcher names the missing one when it needs it.
_zones_note: Ordered, most-likely first, and rendered into the job's resources.any_of. This is an INPUT,
not a fact about the world: SkyPilot's catalog prices some trn2 sizes in exactly one zone,
and which zone has capacity is a property of the account. A run may come back on the second
entry -- which is why the category is derived from IMDS on the instance rather than from
_subnet_note: Recorded and shape-validated, NOT rendered into the job. SkyPilot is not installed on the
desk; it runs on the controller instance, and the subnet it places instances in comes from
the controller's own ~/.sky/config.yaml rather than from a task YAML field. So these two
keys document the venue the run is expected to land in and let the launcher record it in the
manifest; making them take effect is a controller-side change.
How the placement actually resolves, since this note used to say it was unknowable without a
launch: a controller config that pins `aws.vpc_names` selects the VPC by NAME, and SkyPilot
then picks a subnet inside it that is in the zone the job asked for. So `zones` -- which IS
rendered -- is the field that steers placement, and a subnet added to that VPC in a new zone
becomes eligible with no controller change at all. Read the controller's config before
assuming the subnet id below is what takes effect; it is a record, not an instruction.
_controller_note: The SkyPilot controller, reached over SSM. Required only for --launch: without it the
launcher renders and prints the SSM command bodies for someone to run themselves.
controller_region is where the CONTROLLER runs, which is NOT necessarily `region` above --
that one is where the job launches. One controller launches into many regions, and a config
with `use_ssm` reaches the instance without needing to share its network. These were a single
field once, and send-command went to the job's region and got InvalidInstanceId. Defaults to
`region` when unset. An instance id is also not a durable name: controllers get rebuilt, so
--launch checks the id is Online in that region before sending anything.
_repo_url_note: The remote the instance clones, and the remote `git ls-remote` is run against for TASK-N18
constraint 4. Required for any launch: without it there is no way to check that the instance
_image_id_note: Optional. Pinning the DLAMI is the cleanest way to satisfy REQ-088's fourth item; left
unset, the pin depends on the AMI id the instance reports, which sdk_versions.py records
either way. A tolerance derived under one pinned set is not valid under another.
_reference_uri_note: Where TASK-N08 owed step 2's staged GPU reference tensors live. Needed by the c5-parity
profile only. Every file synced from here is sha256-checked against the manifest committed
at verify/neuron/c5_reference_floor_results.json before anything reads it as a reference:
transport moves bytes and confers no integrity.
_venv_preference_note: A substring identifying which of the DLAMI's venvs to activate. Defaults to nxd_inference.
The venv is ACTIVATED with `. <venv>/bin/activate`, never invoked as <venv>/bin/python --
the latter leaves the PJRT plugin path unset, the device count reads zero, and the run looks
like a hardware finding. That broke Phase 0 run 1 (constraint 5). Recording which venv was
active also matters for REQ-095: the two prior NxD import attempts that left it open were
each taken in whichever venv happened to be active.
